The Islamic policy, authored by Ibn Taymiyyah, explores the principles of just governance and leadership within an Islamic framework. The book emphasizes the importance of fulfilling trusts, upholding justice, and adhering to divine commandments in both personal and public life. Key themes include the role of rulers as stewards accountable to Allah, the necessity of appointing capable and trustworthy individuals to positions of authority, and the equitable distribution of wealth according to Islamic law. Ibn Taymiyyah also discusses theSpoils of War (Anfāl) and alms (Sadaqah), highlighting their proper utilization for the benefit of the Muslim community. The text underscores the balance between strength and trustworthiness in leadership, advocating for a governance that reflects both piety and practical wisdom to ensure the welfare of all citizens.
